items.title: Life-saving program for newcomers to Canada proves popular in Mississauga
items.summary: A water safety program for newcomers to Canada that aims to save lives has proven popular in Mississauga, the city says. Nearly 500 people who’ve recently (within the past five years) moved to Canada have enrolled in the City of Mississauga’s Swim to Survive program for newcomers since it was launched in summer 2024, according to city officials. The program, offered free of charge to newcomers in Mississauga, is a Lifesaving Society initiative that seeks to prevent drowning and water-related injuries. ” Swim to Survive teaches “the essential skills every Canadian should know in a water emergency,” officials said. Program open to those ages eight and older The program in Mississauga is open to newcomers ages eight and older. It offers three one-hour classes where participants will learn how to roll into deep water, tread water for one minute and swim 50 metres. “As Mississauga continues to welcome newcomers, the program addresses a critical but often overlooked aspect of settlement — water safety,” city officials say.

items.title: Applications now open for Mississauga’s 2027 Community and Culture Grant programs
items.summary: The grants will support arts, culture, recreation, and community initiatives in Mississauga. m. The City of Mississauga is calling on not-for-profits in need of financial assistance to apply for its Culture and Community Grant Programs for the upcoming year. Funding is available to organizations of all sizes, including small and grassroots groups, looking to expand and support recreational opportunities, local events, arts programming and other community initiatives in Mississauga. Interested organizations can attend a virtual information session and review the grant guidelines on the city’s website. Grant applications must be submitted online by Friday, Oct. m. Not-for-profit community groups can apply for the following grants: The grant is open to non-profit, community-based arts, culture and heritage organizations of all sizes for the development of exemplary arts and culture programs and services, with the objective of improving participation in and appreciation of arts and heritage among Mississauga residents. Available to Mississauga not-for-profit community groups to deliver recreational programs and services, including sports organizations and groups focused on youth, older adults, outdoor recreation, adaptive and inclusive recreation, and more.

items.title: 75 candidates running for city council seats in Mississauga
items.summary: The 14-candidate mayoral race in Mississauga has received plenty of attention as voters prepare to cast their ballots in the 2026 municipal election slated for Oct. 26. Not to be forgotten, a total of 75 candidates — among them nine incumbents — are vying for city council seats in Mississauga’s 11 wards. With current city councillors Alvin Tedjo (Ward 2) and Dipika Damerla (Ward 7) entered in the mayoral contest, that means at least two new faces will join Mississauga council for its next term to begin later this year. Not surprisingly, those two wards also feature the largest fields of candidates in the upcoming election — 17 people are vying for the Ward 7 seat while 14 hopefuls will do battle in Ward 2 (see names of all candidates below). Ward 7 includes the south-central part of Mississauga and is anchored by Cooksville while Ward 2 is comprised of areas in the city’s southwest that include the neighbourhoods of Clarkson and Lorne Park. Ward 5, which includes the Malton area and is historically among the most hotly contested races in the city during election years, offers 10 candidates from which to choose, including incumbent Natalie Hart. Candidate nominations closed this past Friday, so the mayoral and council races are now set. The two highest-profile mayoral candidates — the current mayor, Carolyn Parrish, and her predecessor, Bonnie Crombie — are joined in the contest by Tedjo, Damerla and 10 others of varying experience in the realm of political campaigning.

items.title: Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish slams Trump's 'Lake America' plan as Canada-US trade tensions hit new low
items.summary: Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish responded to US President Donald Trump's "Lake America" idea on Tuesday with a clear message: Keep Lake Ontario's name out of your mouth. Parrish took to X to brush off the president's suggestion, pointing to the region's long Indigenous history and making sure everyone knows just how much the lake means to local communities. Mississauga stands ready to defend local jobs and small and medium-sized businesses at risk from unfair tariffs
items.summary: Staff are examining ways to support jobs while awaiting federal or provincial tariff relief. Today, in light of unfair trade tariffs, Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish met with the President and CEO of the Mississauga Board of Trade David Wojcik, the City’s Acting Chief Administrative Officer, and the Director of Economic Development to map out ways the City can advocate for and support small and medium-sized businesses and jobs disrupted by uncertainty. The suspension of trade negotiations and escalation of US tariff policies against Canada present a significant and ongoing threat to Mississauga’s businesses and workers. Mississauga’s economy is particularly vulnerable to US tariffs: 18 per cent of total employment – roughly 89,000 jobs – is tied directly to US exports. Key areas affected include automotive parts, machinery and electronics, plastics and rubber, furniture, and steel and aluminum products. As a City, we are determined to stand up and defend these jobs and sectors. We are encouraged that the federal government today is rolling out rapid assistance to workers and businesses hit by this latest trade and economic turbulence. These troubling trade developments imperil jobs and risk a spike in inflation. That is why we are exploring ways in which to help our local businesses. 5 million in funding under the federal Regional Tariff Response Initiative (RTRI). Securing this funding would help us deliver a trade mission acceleration program designed to help Mississauga’s small and medium-sized businesses diversify into non-US markets through export readiness training and trade missions. It is clear that we must diversify our international trade partnerships. Mississauga has always been open to the world. That openness will facilitate an expansion of productive and solid international partnerships.

items.title: Mississauga Says Flood Defences Now Protect Over 1,000 Properties Two Years After Historic Storms
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga says more than 1,000 homes and businesses in the hardest-hit part of the city are now better protected from flooding, two years after back-to-back storms devastated parts of the community. INsauga reports the July 16 and August 17-18, 2024 rainstorms together dropped nearly 280 millimetres of rain on Mississauga, with each storm classified as a one-in-100-year event. The outlet notes the city's east end was among the areas hit hardest, with firefighters using rescue boats during the July storm to check on dozens of vehicles stranded in floodwaters near Dundas Street and Dixie Road. According to INsauga, city officials pledged at the time to strengthen existing infrastructure, introduce new practices and add staff to build a more effective defence against future extreme weather. The outlet reports that pledge has translated into tangible protection for the more than 1,000 properties the city says are now safer as a result of the work completed since the 2024 flooding.

items.title: This Week's Featured Listing: A 5,500-Square-Foot Custom Build in Clarkson
items.summary: According to INsauga's House of the Week feature, this week's pick is a custom-built residence at 1031 Welwyn Drive in Clarkson, offering more than 5,500 square feet of living space on a spacious, tree-lined lot. The outlet reports the home is finished with dramatic ceiling heights, skylights, expansive windows, built-in speakers and hand-scraped maple hardwood flooring throughout. INsauga notes the skylights are equipped with rain sensors that automatically close them during wet weather, while the smart speaker system is placed throughout the home to create ambient sound. According to the outlet, the entryway opens into a double-height living space anchored by a floor-to-ceiling stone fireplace, and the kitchen features a Calacatta marble waterfall island, premium built-in appliances and a butler's pantry with heated floors and garage access. INsauga describes a sunlit loft above the living space as a quiet retreat for reading or working beneath the skylights.

items.title: Ontario's Police Watchdog Finds No Grounds for Charges in High Point Mall Arrest Injury
items.summary: According to INsauga, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared Peel Regional Police officers of criminal wrongdoing after a man was seriously injured during an arrest in the parking lot of High Point Mall on Dixie Road in May. INsauga reports the SIU, a civilian agency that investigates police-involved incidents resulting in death, serious injury, firearm discharge or alleged sexual assault, opened its review after officers responded to a report of a stolen 2023 Hyundai Sonata. The outlet reports the vehicle's owner used tracking technology to locate the car in the mall parking lot, where officers found a 33-year-old man in the driver's seat and told him he was under arrest. According to the SIU report cited by INsauga, the man did not get out of the vehicle and held onto the steering wheel as an officer reached in to pull him out, resulting in the injuries under investigation. INsauga reports the SIU ultimately determined there were no reasonable grounds to lay criminal charges against the officers involved.
